best_for: Players who buy or collect indie games on itch.io and want them installed, updated and launched from one place instead of downloading zip files by hand.

points.title: Your itch.io library on the desktop
points.text: The app installs games and tools you own or claimed on itch.io and keeps them updated. Browser games can be synced into the app and played offline.

points.title: You must sign in
points.text: The app cannot be used anonymously. On first launch it opens itch.io in your browser to log in. Buying and downloading on the website still works without an account.

points.title: A sandbox for untrusted games
points.text: The sandbox runs games with fewer rights: as a separate low-privilege user on Windows, and with a per-game home folder on Linux. Saves made inside the sandbox stay there, and it does not guard against graphics driver flaws.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: The app is MIT-licensed and on GitHub. Games keep their own prices; many are only built for one platform, while HTML5 games run on all three.

points.title: Install locations
points.text: You can add extra install folders and pick one as the default, so large games do not fill your system drive.

points.title: Linux updates differently
points.text: On Windows and macOS the app updates itself. On Linux you update through your package manager. The Flatpak here is from Flathub, which does not mark it as verified by itch.io.

points.title: Platform notes
points.text: On Windows it installs for the current user from a zip, with 3 versions kept here. The macOS build needs macOS 13 or newer. macOS and Linux list only the current release.
